[30m[104m ☐ Cache strategy 

[2m[39m[49m│[0m [1m[97mWhich caching strategy should the image proxy use for thumbnails generated on demand, given that the origin is slow 
[0;2m│[0m [1m[97mand the CDN bills per request?

[0m[94m❯[39m [2m[37m1.[0m [94mAggressive CDN caching (Recommended)
[39m     [2m[37mCache thumbnails at the CDN with long TTLs and immutable URLs keyed by size and params. Repeat requests skip the 
[0m     [2m[37mslow origin and cut per-request billing sharply.
[0m  [2m[37m2.[0m Proxy-local disk cache
     [2m[37mStore generated thumbnails on the proxy host's disk and serve from there. Avoids origin hits but still bills every 
[0m     [2m[37mCDN request, and it doesn't scale across proxy instances.
[0m  [2m[37m3.[0m Short TTL with revalidation
     [2m[37mUse short max-age and revalidate with ETags on each expiry. Keeps thumbnails fresh after source edits, but each 
[0m     [2m[37mrevalidation still bills a CDN request and may hit the slow origin.
[0m  [2m[37m4.[0m Pre-generate on upload
     [2m[37mGenerate all thumbnail sizes when the source image is uploaded and store them in object storage. Removes on-demand 
[0m     [2m[37mlatency, but costs storage and wastes work on sizes nobody requests.
[0m  [2m[37m5. [0m[37mType something.
